definitions.explanation: The physical sensation or state of being warm, as opposed to cold.
Emotional warmth — the feeling of kindness, gentleness, or care from a person.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}の{暖|あたた}かさが{気持|きも}ちいい。
examples.english: The warmth of spring feels nice.

examples.japanese: コートのおかげで{暖|あたた}かさを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: Thanks to the coat, I felt warmth.

examples.japanese: {南|みなみ}の{島|しま}の{暖|あたた}かさに{慣|な}れると、{冬|ふゆ}の{日本|にほん}が{辛|つら}くなる。
examples.english: Once you get used to the warmth of a southern island, Japanese winters become hard to bear.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{言葉|ことば}に{暖|あたた}かさを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I felt warmth in her words.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}の{暖|あたた}かさが{恋|こい}しい。
examples.english: I miss the warmth of my family.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}の{暖|あたた}かさに{触|ふ}れて、この{町|まち}に{住|す}みたいと{思|おも}った。
examples.english: Experiencing the warmth of the people here made me want to live in this town.

notes:
Formed from the i-adjective {暖|あたた}かい by replacing い with さ (the standard way to nominalize i-adjectives). Can also be written {温|あたた}かさ, but {暖|あたた}かさ is more common for weather/climate warmth, while {温|あたた}かさ tends to appear for emotional warmth or warm food/drinks. In practice, the two kanji are often interchangeable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {暖|あたた}かさを{感|かん}じる: to feel warmth
- {人|ひと}の{暖|あたた}かさ: human warmth/kindness
- {春|はる}の{暖|あたた}かさ: the warmth of spring

RELATED WORDS:
- {暖|あたた}かい: warm (the adjective form)
- {暑|あつ}さ: heat (summer heat, hot weather)
- {冷|つめ}たさ: coldness (antonym)
